A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Zoom-IQA and GR-IQA work. Their main text and complete supplements support reliable comparison, including matching equations, tables, and qualitative examples across substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original IQA benchmark results, reasoning evaluations, component ablations, and SUPIR/DreamClear restoration examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative restoration, crop-policy and saliency evaluations, human rankings, another model judge, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The backbone, VRF/HACF filtering, two-stage SFT/GRPO training, crop-and-refine procedure, rewards, KL-Coverage regularizer, and progressive resampling remain. Sample-level HACF wording clarifies v1's existing procedure. The total-reward formula moved from v1 Supplement Section 10.1; it is not a new objective.

E1.justification: The seven IQA datasets and existing restoration tasks remain. v3 adds quantitative restoration coverage on synthetic DIV2K and real-world RealLQ250, plus targeted background-bokeh and night-noise examples, including FoundIR. DreamClear itself was already evaluated in v1's supplement.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged, including DeQA renamed DeQA-Score. v3 adds Qwen2.5-VL-7b as a saliency-grounding comparator in Table 6 and central-crop and separately defined single-stage SFT controls in Table 5.

E3.justification: New protocols include quantitative restoration metrics, QAGNet-based crop evaluation using area/SDL/F0.5, Grok-4-1-fast judging, a human-ranking study with 15 annotators on 30 images, and runtime testing. Section 4.1 also changes reported SFT gradient accumulation from eight steps to four; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained component ablations, v3 adds crop-policy and training-paradigm controls, saliency-grounding analysis, independent judge/human checks addressing evaluator self-preference, and background-bokeh/night-noise case studies (Tables 5-7; Figures 14-15). These substantially expand tests of the central mechanism and evaluation validity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed variation, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added human-study sample counts concern evaluation design. The retained Confidence rubric measures assertiveness of language, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-2 and the original component ablation table remain unchanged after matching layouts. Tables 3 and 5-8 add substantial results, including KonIQ PLCC of 0.938 versus 0.898 for central cropping. Restoration findings are mixed: Zoom-IQA leads several perceptual metrics, but SUPIR PSNR is 21.31 versus Q-Insight's 22.44.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1 Supplement Section 10.2's explicit masked GRPO objective (Equation 7), probability-ratio definition, and token-validity-mask definition. The other method equations remain, including the relocated total-reward formula. This reduces formal specification without establishing an algorithm change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: GR-IQA, interactive region-aware Zoom-IQA, KL-Coverage and resampling, and claims of reliable reasoning, generalization, and downstream usefulness. Added evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: New discussions interpret learned cropping versus fixed cropping, semantic grounding of selected regions, and RL versus supervised imitation. The supplement additionally addresses evaluator self-preference, artistic bokeh versus defects, background noise, and deployment latency. These introduce substantive mechanism explanations and applicability arguments absent from v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds timing hardware/software information (NVIDIA H200 NVL and vLLM) and revises SFT accumulation steps. It removes the disclosed score-reward sigma of 0.35, detailed GRPO/token-masking specification, and identification of SwinIR in restoration preprocessing. Prompt templates, filtering thresholds, reward weights, and the project link remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds brief discussion of VQ-Insight and Reasoning as Representation. Other new citations support saliency, runtime, and restoration evaluation, while DeepSeekMath and SwinIR citations disappear. The central positioning against non-interactive, text-only IQA reasoning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 revises VRF/HACF explanations, moves existing restoration and total-reward material into the main text, and adds discussion sections, an author, and acknowledgments. Most existing abstract, introduction, results interpretation, and conclusion prose remains, so language and narrative restructuring are limited.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. Existing result tables are reorganized into stacked metric or dataset blocks, figures are resized and relocated, and captions are revised. Five new result tables and Figures 14-15 substantially expand the displays; original supplementary examples are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The crop-policy controls, saliency evaluation, and independent Grok/human assessments substantially strengthen validation of the central region-aware reasoning claim beyond v1's component ablations, model judges, and examples. Quantitative restoration results also expose metric-dependent tradeoffs. These gains outweigh the loss of some GRPO and reproducibility details, although the human study is small and statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
